Simulation and validation

Compare the clocks.
Keep the scale honest.

A link-dependent timestamp model, more than 1.5 million nonlinear grid trials and explicit checks against the local covariance prediction. All results remain conditional simulations.

Reproducible model v2.0

The same colour
means the same error.

Only the clock setting changes between these two Monte Carlo maps. A third map reports their improvement directly.

Different patterns are not a requirement for correctness. The earlier uniform-error maps were scalar multiples. This model adds declared link-dependent noise and correlated propagation terms. Their influence is tested numerically, rather than added for visual effect.

Local covariance meets nonlinear estimation.

LocationClock RMSPredicted RMSSimulated RMSSimulated radial R95

12,000 trials per representative position and clock setting. Estimated positions are unconstrained. Solver convergence and relative agreement checks are supplied with the downloadable data.

Precision has a floor.
Bias survives averaging.

Clock improvements eventually meet receiver and calibration limits. Repeated bursts from one installation also share slow errors.

A fixed installation

One installation keeps the same clock and calibration offsets across repeated bursts. Its mean position can remain biased even as the cloud of individual fixes becomes tight.

An unmodelled 3 ns delay

An added positive delay at BS3 is a deliberate model-mismatch test. The solver does not know the bias. A small fitted residual alone cannot guarantee an honest position.

What was verified.

  • Python and browser covariance agree for the default example.
  • Nonlinear solutions start from a data-driven coarse search.
  • Failed convergence is counted; estimated coordinates are never clipped.
  • Static offsets are held fixed in repeatability trials.
  • Coverage assumptions are separate from numerical solver success.

These checks validate the implementation of the chosen timestamp model. They do not validate an RF waveform, an optical clock servo, a real site or a product.
